answer: One agent, one titled parcel: the land registry signs a fresh challenge binding the agent's key to a single registered deed, kept on the public record's ledge and re-checked against the cadastre every epoch. A second key claiming the same parcel is rejected outright, since the registry holds the title record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 parcels at roughly $2,000 each all-in — about $2,000,000 — plus 1,000 real owners on the public record, a delta of cost no script can fake, and any deed can be revoked the moment fraud is found, stranding the attacker in a lagoon of dead titles.
